classification.difficultyReason: The hardest demand is discovering, without a construction hint, that four alternate parallelepiped vertices form a tetrahedron whose edges are face diagonals. The midpoint construction also requires spatial interpretation to recognise the resulting octahedron.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw two tetrahedrons joined at a base. Describe the polyhedron you get. Calculate $V-E+F$ for this polyhedron.

answer.short: A triangular dipyramid with 6 triangular faces, 9 edges and 5 vertices. $V-E+F=5-9+6=2$.
answer.worked:
Join the tetrahedrons along a common triangular base. The common base is inside the solid, leaving six triangular faces. There are three vertices around the join and two apexes, giving five vertices. The three edges around the join and six edges to the apexes give nine edges.

$$V-E+F=5-9+6=2.$$

spec.description: Two tetrahedrons sharing a triangular base, forming a triangular dipyramid. The rear lower edge is dashed.
spec.mathematics: Five vertices, nine edges and six exterior triangular faces; the common triangular base is internal.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A parallelepiped is a prism with all faces a parallelogram. Draw a parallelepiped.

answer.short: A prism with all six faces parallelograms, as shown.
answer.worked: Draw two congruent, parallel parallelograms. Join corresponding vertices with parallel edges; show hidden edges dashed. Each of the six faces is a parallelogram.

spec.description: An oblique parallelepiped with six parallelogram faces and three dashed rear edges.
spec.mathematics: Opposite faces are congruent and parallel; all faces are parallelograms.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show how a tetrahedron can be inscribed in a parallelepiped with each edge of the tetrahedron lying on a face of the parallelepiped.

answer.short: Join four alternate vertices of the parallelepiped. The six edges of the tetrahedron are diagonals of its six faces.
answer.worked: Choose four alternate vertices of the parallelepiped, so no two chosen vertices are joined by an edge of the parallelepiped. Join every pair of chosen vertices. Each of these six joins is a diagonal of one face, forming the required tetrahedron.

spec.description: A parallelepiped with a tetrahedron joining four alternate vertices. Thin outlines identify the containing solid and heavier diagonals identify the tetrahedron.
spec.mathematics: The six tetrahedron edges lie respectively on the front, right, top, bottom, back and left faces.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find, by means of a rough sketch, what polyhedron has its vertices at the midpoints of the edges of a tetrahedron.

answer.worked: Mark the midpoint of each of the six edges of the tetrahedron. On each triangular face, join its three edge midpoints. The resulting solid has six vertices and eight triangular faces, so it is an octahedron.

spec.description: A tetrahedron with its six edge midpoints marked and joined to form an inscribed octahedron. The front midpoint triangle is solid; edges behind the front face are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Each midpoint joins the four midpoints on adjacent original edges, producing twelve edges and eight triangular faces.
